summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with a flare of chronic pancreatitis and associated epigastric pain radiating to the back, along with nausea, vomiting, and inability to tolerate J-tube feeds. She also reported atypical chest pain radiating to the left arm, which was exacerbated by nausea and vomiting but relieved by sublingual nitroglycerin. Workup showed no cardiac ischemia, with normal EKGs and negative troponins, suggesting the chest pain may have been due to esophageal spasm. She was managed with IV fluids, pain control using Dilaudid, Ativan, and Phenergan per her established protocol, and NPO status. A PICC line was placed on hospital day three for reliable IV access. Her symptoms improved over five days, she resumed J-tube feeds, and was discharged on her baseline medications with follow-up arranged. No further chest pain occurred after admission day one.
